steps.text: This looks clearly malicious — an Empire-style AMSI bypass with an encoded payload hidden in a Debug value, triggered via a Run key. I should pull the related registry entities, network connections, and parent process to trace the full chain.

The process also created registry keys over and over (11 times). At 2020-07-22 04:19:04 it wrote a base64 PowerShell payload into the value HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Debug. The decoded start of the payload is an Empire-style script that tampers with PowerShell's group-policy logging settings (cachedGroupPolicySettings) to avoid being logged. That value reads the Debug value and runs it as 'powershell -Win Hidden -enc' at every logon, so this is fileless persistence that starts a hidden encoded script. submission.reasoning: This is malicious. On workstation5.mordor.local, powershell.exe (proc-8b801b5203) running as MORDOR\pgustavo connected to 10.10.10.5:80 (10 times from 04:18:48). At 2020-07-22 04:19:04 it wrote a base64 PowerShell payload into HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Debug. The decoded start is an Empire-style script that tampers with PowerShell group-policy logging settings. Then it set the Run key value HKLM\...\CurrentVersion\Run\Updater, which reads the Debug value and runs it as 'powershell -Win Hidden -enc' at every logon: fileless persistence. Response: isolate the host, delete both values, block 10.10.10.5, rotate pgustavo's credentials, and check the other key the process created (reg-d91a9c1c29), which was not opened.
